title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Des Moines, IA: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Des Moines equipment, tank, datacenter and Iowa DOT bridge welding: Part C code choice, Part B travel and AWS eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Des Moines: Six Days for Central Iowa Equipment, Tank, Datacenter and Bridge Welding Inspectors
html:
Central Iowa builds a great deal of heavy steel. Farm and utility equipment comes out of plants around the metro, storage tank plate is fabricated in Clive, the Iowa Department of Transportation is rebuilding the Mixmaster interchanges that carry I-35, I-80 and I-235 through Des Moines, and Microsoft is putting up more datacenter buildings in West Des Moines. Each of those jobs has welds that someone has to accept against a code, a drawing or a contract specification, and the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) is the credential that owners, buyers and testing agencies recognize for that role.

Atlantis NDT prepares candidates for the CWI examination with a six-day course aimed at welders, fitters, quality technicians, NDT technicians and engineers in and around Polk County. The American Welding Society writes and administers the examination and issues the certification; you apply to AWS yourself and meet its education, experience and vision requirements in your own name. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis does not see examination content. There is no Atlantis classroom in Des Moines. You can work through the six days online at your own pace with an instructor answering your questions, an employer can have them delivered at its plant for a group, or you can book one-to-one sessions online or in person at a location agreed when you book. The full outline is on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

Who asks for a CWI around Des Moines

The table maps the main sources of welding inspection work in the metro to the document that usually governs the welds. Treat it as a starting point: the contract or drawing always has the final word.

WorkExample in central IowaDocument that usually governs
Agricultural and utility equipmentJohn Deere Des Moines Works; the new Vermeer plant in BondurantManufacturer drawings and internal weld standards, with AWS D1.1 where the drawing calls it up
Welded steel storage tanksThe CB&I fabrication facility in CliveAPI 650 or the owner's tank specification, with ASME Section IX for procedure and welder qualification
Highway bridges, signs and lightingIowa DOT Northeast and Southwest Mixmaster workAWS D1.5 for bridge members and AWS D1.1 for signal, sign and lighting supports (Iowa DOT Materials IM 557)
Data center buildingsMicrosoft datacenter construction in West Des MoinesAWS D1.1 for structural steel; the project piping specification for mechanical systems
Wind and powerWind generated 66 percent of Iowa's electricity in 2024Owner and manufacturer specifications, with D1.1 for ancillary structural steel

Equipment plants: windrowers moving in, a Vermeer site going up

Deere said in November 2026 that it would close Ottumwa Works and stop manufacturing at its Hagie plant in Clarion as part of a restructuring. Windrower production is due to move from Ottumwa to Des Moines Works by the end of fiscal 2027, and round balers are to follow by the end of 2028, according to DTN and AgWeb. A product line arriving at a plant brings new weldments, new fixtures and new first-article inspections, which is exactly the work a quality department wants a certified inspector to own.

Pella-based Vermeer announced in February 2026 an all-new 300,000-square-foot facility in Bondurant with machining, weld, paint and assembly, more than 300 jobs at the outset and a focus on products from its utility, tree care and landscape lines, and the company broke ground there in May 2026. A plant built from nothing has to write its weld inspection plan, train people to it and show customers it works. Many equipment welds are fillet and groove welds made with gas metal arc or flux cored arc welding, a good share of them by robots, and the inspector checks size, profile, location, undercut and porosity against the drawing.

Iowa DOT rules for steel fabrication shops

Iowa DOT approves the shops that fabricate steel for state projects under Materials IM 557, revised in October 2020. For bridge components in its groups 1 and 2a, welding procedures and requirements must conform to the AWS D1.5 Bridge Welding Code, while traffic signal, sign support, lighting and pre-engineered truss trail bridge components follow AWS D1.1. AISC quality certification is one basis for approval, though not for the bridge components category. The IM also allows a fabricator to use certified welding inspectors supplied by a testing agency as its in-house inspector, provided they document experience with welding procedure specifications, bridge component assembly, tolerances, surface preparation and painting.

Materials IM 561, on shop welding inspection, makes the fabricator's quality control responsible for checking and recording fabrication according to AWS, with quality assurance on main member fabrication provided by an Iowa DOT representative. Volumetric testing on that work comes from a certified independent third-party firm, and NDT personnel are qualified under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. For a Des Moines candidate, that adds up to two places a CWI fits on state steel: in a fabricator's quality department, or with a testing agency placed in the shop.

The interchanges being rebuilt around the city

Two Iowa DOT programs dominate interstate work in the metro. The Northeast Mixmaster has been under reconstruction in phases since 2008: new bridges went in at NE 29th Street and Fourmile Creek, eastbound traffic moved onto the old westbound lanes in 2026 while the old eastbound lanes were rebuilt, and the NE 38th Street bridge over I-80 is planned to be rebuilt over the winter of 2026 to 2027. The Southwest Mixmaster, the I-35/I-80/I-235 interchange in the West Des Moines area, runs from 2026 through 2029 and replaces loop and directional ramps with new flyover bridges, beginning with piers for the future flyover in 2026.

Whether a given flyover uses steel or concrete girders is a design decision made bridge by bridge. Either way, programs of this size bring bearings, expansion joints, barrier and sign structures, and contractors who need inspectors familiar with the D1.5 and D1.1 split described above. Background: AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code.

Datacenters in West Des Moines

Microsoft already runs datacenters in West Des Moines and is building more there. Its October 2025 fact sheet counted about 540 people working at the operating sites and estimated more than 1,660 jobs at peak construction activity on the new facilities, around 6.8 million work hours in all. The company's construction update for its Ginger West datacenter names Turner Construction as general contractor and estimates completion by summer 2028. The same fact sheet describes a Datacenter Academy run with Des Moines Area Community College, which had 313 students enrolled in 2024 to 2025.

For a welding inspector, a datacenter campus is mostly a building job: structural steel frames and platforms erected to AWS D1.1, embeds and miscellaneous metals, and large mechanical piping systems for cooling whose welding requirements come from the project specification. People who can read both a structural drawing and a piping specification are useful to the erectors, mechanical contractors and testing agencies on those sites. Related: NDT training for data center construction.

Tank plate in Clive, and the API 650 question

CB&I lists a fabrication facility in Clive, Iowa, as one of two, with Houston, that support regional projects for its Americas operations, and its Storage Solutions business builds welded tanks. The AWS Iowa Section announced a tour of the Clive facility for November 5, 2026. New welded tanks are built to API 650 and in-service tanks are inspected and repaired under API 653, with procedures and welders qualified to ASME Section IX.

Neither API 650 nor API 653 is on the AWS list of Part C code books. A tank fabricator's candidate therefore chooses between the ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, which lines up with the qualification side of tank work, and AWS D1.1, which suits stairways, platforms and roof framing. Inspectors who stay in tank work often add API 653 later; Atlantis offers self-paced API exam preparation, and API administers that examination and certifies its inspectors. Background: API 653 tank inspection guide.

Wind on the grid, steel in the field

Wind provided 66 percent of Iowa's electricity in 2024, according to the Iowa Environmental Council, and it has been the state's leading source of power since passing coal in 2019. Turbine towers and nacelles are welded in factories to their makers' specifications. Field and support steel around wind farms and their grid connections, such as substation structures, platforms and access ladders, is where AWS D1.1 commonly applies unless the owner's specification says otherwise, so a Des Moines CWI who wants energy work should read the owner documents as carefully as the code.

Pick the Part C book from the job you want next

Part C is an open-book test on one code book that you choose when you apply. Choose for the work you expect to do for the next several years, not for what seems easiest on exam day.

If your next job looks like thisConsiderWhy
Equipment plant or fabrication shop qualityAWS D1.1:2020The general structural welding code for carbon and low-alloy steel
Bridge girders and Iowa DOT fabricationAWS D1.5:2020, including Clause 12Iowa DOT requires D1.5 for its group 1 and 2a bridge components
Tanks, process piping, boilersASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3The qualification and piping rules tank and plant contracts cite
Aluminum trailers, platforms and equipment partsAWS D1.2:2014The structural aluminum code on the AWS list
Gas distribution or pipeline contractorsAPI 1104, 22nd editionPipeline girth welds, their qualification and acceptance

The AWS list names specific editions, which can trail the newest one in print, so study the edition AWS names for your examination. Background: AWS D1.1 and WPS, PQR and WPQ explained.

Where central Iowa welders learn and meet

Des Moines Area Community College teaches welding through the Iowa Welding Institute at DMACC. The welding certificate curriculum covers oxyacetylene welding, brazing and cutting; shielded metal arc welding, basic and structural; flux cored and gas metal arc welding; gas tungsten arc welding; and blueprint reading for welders and fitters, on carbon steel, stainless steel and aluminum in all positions, with 2-inch pipe welds in 5G and 6G. The stick courses list AWS QC10 2G and 3G qualification tests.

Ironworkers Local 67 in Des Moines trains structural ironworkers through its apprenticeship, which Iowa Workforce Development featured in February 2025. The AWS Iowa Section, Section 066 in District 16, runs technical events, plant tours and an annual memorial golf outing whose May 2026 recap counted 78 attendees, with Indian Hills Community College and Iowa Central Community College among its sponsors; the Eastern Iowa Section covers the other end of the state. Section events are a practical way to meet working CWIs who can tell you which code books local employers favor and who may later verify your experience.

Part B means leaving Iowa

AWS delivers Parts A and C as computer-based tests at Prometric centers and gives Part B, the practical, only at its educational seminar locations. The AWS list of CWI training locations in November 2026 had nothing in Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri or Nebraska. The listed sites a Des Moines candidate would usually compare are Chicago, Milwaukee, Indianapolis and Detroit to the east, with Tulsa and Denver as alternatives. The Hobart Institute of Welding Technology in Troy, Ohio, also publishes a 2026 list of its CWI preparation sessions carrying AWS exam site codes for Part B; ask AWS whether a session is open to you before planning around it.

For a US Part B date, AWS stops taking applications six weeks beforehand, so the application, the vision record and the experience evidence all need to be ready before you book travel. AWS requires 72 percent on each part, and a sensible budget includes the possibility of one retake. The CWI exam budget calculator helps add travel and time off to the plan.

Counting experience: a central Iowa example

Take a hypothetical candidate who finished the DMACC welding certificate, then spent three years welding frames on an equipment line and two more as a lead hand checking first-piece welds and keeping weld records. Completed trade or vocational courses reduce the AWS experience requirement to four years, so on paper this person qualifies, but only if AWS accepts the work as welding-related and someone can verify it. That judgment belongs to AWS, not to the employer and not to Atlantis.

Make the case easy to check. List each employer with dates, the processes and materials you welded, the drawings or codes the work followed, and any inspection duties such as dimensional checks, fillet gauging or witnessing welder tests, each with a name that can confirm it. Keep copies of welder qualification records from school and from employers. Then have the vision test done on AWS's visual acuity form by one of the professionals the form lists, timed so it is still current on exam day. The CWI requirements guide covers the full education table.

Six days inside a Polk County plant

An employer with several people heading for the exam can host the course at its own site. For an equipment maker, the practical work uses real production weldments and rejects, the plant's own fillet gauges and its weld drawings; for a bridge or tank fabricator, the code work runs in D1.5 or the ASME option alongside the shop's procedure qualification records. The employer chooses the weeks, so the course can stay clear of a product launch or a line move.

Each person in the group still applies to AWS individually, supplies their own vision record and experience evidence, and sits every part of the exam in their own name. The company can pay for the preparation; it cannot hold the certification.

After the CWI in central Iowa

A new CWI around Des Moines might take over first-article and weld audit duties at an equipment plant, inspect bridge components for a fabricator on Iowa DOT work, or join a testing agency on building and datacenter steel. Inspectors who also want to carry out nondestructive testing need method training and certification by their employer under its written practice; Atlantis provides training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, including VT Level 2, MT Level 2 and UT Level 2, and the employer certifies the technician afterwards. AWS renews the CWI every three years and requires recertification at nine.

Nearby pages: NDT training in Des Moines, NDT training in Iowa, Practical NDT from Des Moines, and CWI exam prep in Omaha, Kansas City and Minneapolis.

Sending a Des Moines enquiry

Tell us who the course is for, which of the three formats you want, the code book you expect to use for Part C and the season in which you plan to sit Part B. For a group, give the plant or yard location and the weeks that suit production. If you are unsure whether your experience will satisfy AWS, describe it in a few lines and we will point out what to confirm with AWS before you start. We quote fees on request and reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Des Moines?
faq.a: The AWS Iowa Section, Section 066 in District 16, holds events in the metro, including a tour of the CB&I fabrication facility in Clive announced for November 2026. The Eastern Iowa Section serves the other end of the state.

faq.q: Where would a Des Moines candidate take Part B?
faq.a: At an AWS seminar location outside Iowa. The November 2026 AWS list had no site in Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri or Nebraska; Chicago, Milwaukee, Indianapolis, Detroit, Tulsa and Denver were listed. Parts A and C are computer-based at Prometric centers.

faq.q: Does Iowa DOT require a CWI on bridge fabrication?
faq.a: Materials IM 557 does not name the AWS CWI, but it lets a fabricator use certified welding inspectors supplied by a testing agency as its in-house inspector if they document relevant experience, and it requires AWS D1.5 for group 1 and 2a bridge components. Check the contract for the exact requirement.

faq.q: Can I use API 650 for Part C?
faq.a: No. API 650 is not on the AWS list of Part C code books. Tank fabrication candidates usually choose the ASME option (Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3) or AWS D1.1.

faq.q: Which code suits an inspector at a farm or utility equipment plant?
faq.a: AWS D1.1 in most cases, because it is the general structural steel welding code and the closest fit to welded frames and weldments. If the plant welds a lot of aluminum, AWS D1.2 is also on the list.

faq.q: I finished the DMACC welding certificate. How much experience must I show?
faq.a: AWS lists four years of welding-related experience for candidates who completed trade or vocational courses. AWS decides whether a course and your work qualify, so describe both clearly in the application.

faq.q: Can a West Des Moines contractor have the six days delivered at its site?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format brings the six days to the employer's facility for a group, using its welds and gauges. Each person still applies to AWS individually.

faq.q: Is the course approved by AWS?
faq.a: No. AWS has not approved or endorsed it, and Atlantis has no access to examination content. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Des Moines?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Des Moines. The course is taken online, at the employer's site for a group, or one-to-one online or in person at a location agreed when booking. Atlantis offices are in Houston and Hyderabad.

faq.q: How do I ask for a quote?
faq.a: Use the enquiry link on this page and tell us the format, the number of candidates and the Part C code you expect to use. There is no published fee: we quote for the format and group size you describe, and we reply within one business day.
